propositions: A single pending entry in the enrich queue disables the O(1) fast path marker optimization store-wide, forcing a full directory walk on every subsequent write (linear in store size, ~1.2s at 4,938 tickets).
The gate marker write logic is all-or-nothing: it only writes when the pending set is empty, so any pending work leaves the marker stale and forces expensive full scans.
The marker should be generalized from whole-store quiet to outside-live-set quiet by recording which ticket ids had live queue entries when the last full scan ran.
Scoped probes using the live set should reduce only those entries (O(backlog), not O(store)), without rewriting the marker so the TTL remains measured from the last full walk.
Every queue append must still invalidate the marker, and wrong-typed live fields must be distrusted, degrading to full scan (honesty rules preserved).

New tests must verify standing-backlog cost via syscall count (not wall clock), new-enqueue visibility, TTL bounds, live-field validation, time-driven transitions, and service-order parity with full walks.
